extracts.quote: We chose Titan because it was getting to a stage where our clinical work, through our services, was being really compromised by the level of dispensing work that we had, so we had to find a different way of working.
extracts.context: Abel explaining why his pharmacy switched to Titan -- services were suffering under dispensing pressure.

extracts.quote: The other day, I was able to have four or five long consultations with patients without having to worry about prescriptions being checked.
extracts.context: Abel describing the immediate impact of Titan on his ability to deliver clinical services uninterrupted.

extracts.quote: The ability to check a prescription allows somebody else to complete it without having to completely bag it and finish it start to finish. That allows our customers to get what they need and leave, whilst allowing me to focus on patients with more complex needs.
extracts.context: Abel explaining how Titan's split workflow between checking and packaging frees the pharmacist.

extracts.quote: I played around properly and I was like, this is bloody good, isn't it? So easy and simple. And now, probably in the whole pharmacy, I know the software the best. The thing with the software is it's constantly evolving and changing. You love it because you have different changes. You see the speed is increasing, and it's stuff you can use, it's useful stuff.
extracts.context: Akbar's unscripted opening to the interview, describing his genuine delight in learning and mastering Titan.

extracts.quote: Without Titan, I don't think I'd be able to step away. I think I'd have to be a lot more hands on, observe everything, look at every process. It allows me to focus on strategic moves rather than just be involved in the day to day. If you're involved in the day to day, you'll never grow.
extracts.context: Akbar explaining how Titan freed him from operational micromanagement to focus on business strategy and growth.

extracts.quote: I didn't imagine it'd be a thing. I always thought I was the most valuable person. Stepping back without things falling apart. Titan gives you the confidence to be able to do that.
extracts.context: Akbar reflecting on his surprise that he could actually step away from day-to-day operations without the pharmacy deteriorating.

extracts.quote: We are a 32,000 item pharmacy per month. That's four times more than most pharmacies. We're doing near 2,000 items a day, but we finish everything. The owings are normally 30 on a Monday, by the end of the week you'll have two.
extracts.context: Akbar establishing the extreme volume of Drayton Prime to contextualize how Titan handles scale, with owings as a quality metric.

extracts.quote: Titan PMR was adopted four years ago, and if you look back on our figures, you'll see the difference. It springs up almost instantaneously. It doubles. We went from 16,000 to 32,000 items.
extracts.context: Akbar attributing a doubling of monthly prescription volume directly to Titan adoption, visible in their business figures.

extracts.quote: I remember early days with ProScript. We had owings galore, like 200 owings. And the owings used to have a bag with the prescription tied to it. You had to trawl through 200 bags. You'd find one and you'd be like, knowing God, am I going to tell this person?
extracts.context: Akbar recalling the nightmare of managing physical owing bags under ProScript, the dread of facing patients when items couldn't be found.

extracts.quote: The one that I would say we take for granted but it's probably the most essential part is location of prescription. You can find a prescription on Titan within 30 seconds and people have confidence in that. They love that. You can tell everyone exactly where their prescription is.
extracts.context: Akbar highlighting prescription tracking as Titan's most underrated feature, enabling confident patient communication.

extracts.quote: Just last week, one of the guys switched Titan AI on and he said, my day's been so much easier. He had used it early on and had a negative block on it. He tried it again and said, fantastic, it's actually really good. You kind of change haters into believers.
extracts.context: Akbar describing a pharmacist who initially resisted Titan AI but was converted after a single day of use.

extracts.quote: With ProScript, you have to have eyes at the back of your head. You can print off a script, print off the label, and it's untrackable. It will disappear. You don't know what's happened with it until the customer comes. Then you're in big trouble.
extracts.context: Akbar contrasting ProScript's lack of prescription tracking with Titan's full audit trail and visibility.

extracts.quote: With Titan, you can search it on the system. You know whether someone's messed up. You can track a prescription and tie it in. It's got a good audit trail and there's nowhere to hide. That is fantastic from my point of view because I can give the customer confidence.
extracts.context: Akbar praising the audit trail as a management and patient-confidence tool, contrasting it with the untraceable nature of ProScript.

extracts.quote: If you don't have a plan, someone's going to come in and destroy your business. They're going to have the plan and you're going to be part of their plan.
extracts.context: Akbar giving blunt business advice about the necessity of strategic planning, with technology as a core tool.

extracts.quote: Boots are paper-based, not going forward. Rowland's are paper-based, not going forward. They're not looking at efficiencies. Times have changed. In 50 years the technology has changed all the way through. So why are we still paper-based? I don't understand it.
extracts.context: Akbar expressing genuine bewilderment that major chains remain on paper systems while independent pharmacies using Titan are outpacing them.

extracts.quote: I don't want anyone to get Titan. Stay paper-based, stay in your zone, because we can take over, and we're happy to take over.
extracts.context: Akbar joking that he actively wants competitors to stay on old systems so Drayton Prime can continue gaining market share.

extracts.quote: The choice was robot or Titan. I looked at it and I weighed it out, and I thought, I don't need a 300,000 pound robot. I've got Titan. It does the job for me per day.
extracts.context: Akbar explaining his capital allocation decision: Titan replaced both a refit and a dispensing robot in terms of efficiency gains.

extracts.quote: It probably saves or makes up for three or four staff members. Before we used to have a lot more staff members. After implementing Titan, I can comfortably say we've saved three full-time members of staff.
extracts.context: Akbar quantifying Titan's labor-equivalent value, estimating three to four full-time staff savings.

extracts.quote: I can comfortably say that we've saved three full-time members of staff. That's a saving in itself. Titan offers you savings you can't see.
extracts.context: Akbar quantifying the hidden labor savings from Titan, equating workflow efficiency to eliminating three full-time salary costs.

extracts.quote: We do the most Pharmacy First in the area. And NMS, we grew into it after Titanverse. Before Titanverse we weren't, but after Titanverse we were. We get near 300 to 350 NMS done per month.
extracts.context: Akbar attributing their NMS volume growth directly to Titanverse adoption, establishing them as area leaders.

extracts.quote: Before Titan, you'd be there till two o'clock in the morning. And I had a staff member who turned around and said, this is hell. Then a month after we got Titan, they looked at me and said, we can go home on time.
extracts.context: Akbar recounting the dramatic shift in working hours at Drayton Prime, from post-midnight finishes to leaving on schedule.

extracts.quote: Drayton Prime is a modern pharmacy that runs whether you're there or you're not there. Just gets the job done. And that's mainly down to the system and the staff who operate the system.
extracts.context: Akbar summarizing the operational independence his pharmacy has achieved with Titan.

extracts.quote: Having spoken to that guy recently, he said, I will never go back to staying after hours. I will never go back to that. And I said to him, you're right, because Drayton Prime is a modern pharmacy that runs whether you're there or not.
extracts.context: Akbar quoting a staff member's reaction about never returning to the pre-Titan era of extreme overtime.

extracts.quote: If you're looking to switch to Titan, it's a hands-on approach. You need to start doing it all yourself. Make sure you're involved and you're able to look at all the steps so that you can train anyone afterwards. Once you know the system and you can train everyone else, then you can step back.
extracts.context: Akbar giving practical implementation advice for new Titan adopters, emphasizing owner involvement in the initial learning phase.

extracts.quote: It's brilliant, it's paperless, it's automated, and it's convenient because you can log in remotely. The clinical checks are easy. I'll tell everyone looking for a PMR system, look at Titan.
extracts.context: Alta from Farm Chemist delivering a concise, camera-ready endorsement of Titan's key selling points.

extracts.quote: I like the Owings. They're a lot easier than the old system. I'll be able to do them a lot quicker. Do you miss the old PMR system? Not anymore. No, I did at the beginning, but not now.
extracts.context: Amanda, a dispenser, describing how she's moved past the initial adjustment period from her old PMR.

extracts.quote: We had the Easter period where we've probably lost about 50 hours of staff per week, and we had three bank holidays in quick succession, and we're doing a 10,000 item pharmacy, and we didn't hit a road bump. extracts.context: Andy describing how his 10,000-item pharmacy survived Easter bank holidays with 50 hours less staff per week, crediting Titan. Also in post transcript.

extracts.quote: Introduction of Batch Flow has made a huge difference. Just being able to get all the 1-2-3 item scripts and get them done with just a couple of trips around the dispensary. extracts.context: Andy quantifying the productivity impact of Batch Flow at his multi-site group. Also in post transcript.

extracts.quote: We chose Titan because we needed to move into a service-based business. We needed to move away from the pharmacist being bogged down with checking every single prescription. extracts.context: Andy articulating the strategic business rationale for choosing Titan, framing it as a necessary pivot from dispensing-centric to services-centric pharmacy.

extracts.quote: Pharmacists are only having to be involved in about 20% of the accuracy checks. And with Titan X, their involvement in the clinical checks is assisted as well, and that's only going to get better as Titan X picks up its percentage.

extracts.quote: One of the things that's made a real difference is the way Titan manages electronic repeat dispensing. It automatically schedules downloads for every four weeks. extracts.context: Andy, a multi-site pharmacy owner rolling out across multiple branches, highlighting eRD management as his favourite feature for reducing phone call volume.

extracts.quote: Learning to use Titan at a basic level is like learning to use a Sainsbury's self checkout. It's really intuitive. Use the onboarding videos for the simple stuff. What you really want from your trainer is to take people from 70% to 95%.
extracts.context: Andy sharing practical implementation advice after rolling out Titan across multiple branches, arguing that the intuitive design means trainers should focus on advanced features, not basics.

extracts.quote: We had the Easter period where we lost about 50 hours of staff per week, and we had three bank holidays in quick succession, and we're doing a 10,000 item pharmacy. We didn't hit a rope. It literally went as smooth as it ever has been. The staff put that down to Titan.
extracts.context: Andy describing how a 10,000-item pharmacy survived Easter bank holidays with 50 fewer staff hours per week and still ran smoothly, crediting the Titan workflow.

extracts.quote: The introduction of batch flow has made a huge difference. Just being able to get all the one, two, three item scripts done with just a couple of trips around the dispensary. You can dispense a couple of hundred items with one member of staff in the morning.
extracts.context: Andy describing how batch flow transformed dispensary efficiency at his sites, enabling a single staff member to process hundreds of items in one session.

extracts.quote: As a pharmacist myself, I've seen less work coming towards my way. So I'm able to do more services. It's working out pretty well.
extracts.context: Anoop, on his eighth Titan pharmacy, describing how the system reduces his dispensary workload.

extracts.quote: I was dreading coming in today, but it's gone so smoothly. I'm normally used to ProScript, which is really fiddly, but oh my gosh, this Titan has made things so much easier. Normally I'm a quite stressed person, so this has alleviated part of it and it's just so much better.
extracts.context: Ashley, a dispenser on her first go-live day with Titan at an Avicenna branch, expressing surprise at how much smoother the experience was compared to her expectations and previous ProScript experience.

extracts.quote: Before it was non-stop, baskets piling up. I'd do a travel job in here, then run to the back in between my jobs, start checking, bagging, getting them on the shelf, then running back in here for my next appointment. Back and forth, constantly. I was rushing to check, I was rushing to bag. I was worried that I'm going to make a mistake, and inevitably, at some point, mistakes did happen.
extracts.context: Asif describing daily workflow before Titan at a pharmacy doing 14,500 items/month with ProScript

extracts.quote: I couldn't see across the room because there were baskets.
extracts.context: Asif describing the physical chaos of a busy dispensary running on ProScript before Titan

extracts.quote: It has made my life so much better. If I had hair before, I'd pull it out. Now I can start growing my hair again.
extracts.context: Asif reflecting on personal stress reduction after switching from ProScript to Titan

extracts.quote: I've just had four new staff start. They've been here a week. They've taken to it like a duck to water. Very user friendly. It's not rocket science.
extracts.context: Asif describing how quickly new staff learn Titan with minimal training

extracts.quote: When we had Titan X, it would check around 30 to 40% of my clinical checks. The new Titan AI is going to be checking 80 to 90% of your prescriptions.
extracts.context: Asif comparing Titan X (earlier version) to the new Titan AI for clinical checking automation rates

extracts.quote: We would have between five to six near misses a month easily on ProScript. I've had two since we've had Titan, and that's in a year. And they were human errors, not Titan making an error.
extracts.context: Asif comparing dispensing error rates between ProScript and Titan at a 14,500 items/month pharmacy

extracts.quote: With Titan, all those fears are gone. I literally have no fears as to what my staff are doing, because I know that everything is being scanned. If it's the wrong product, they simply won't get a bag label. If they've missed a product, they won't get the bag label to seal the bag.
extracts.context: Asif explaining how barcode scanning eliminates the worry of staff dispensing errors

extracts.quote: Every other company was comparing themselves to Titan. They would all come to me and say, 'But does Titan do this, Titan doesn't do that.' I'm like, Titan's obviously doing something right that you feel you need to compare your system to Titan. I'm not going to go for an Aldi knock-off. I'm going for the original thing.
extracts.context: Asif explaining why he chose Titan over ProScript, PharmacyX, and Apotek despite sales pressure from competitors

extracts.quote: I said the exact same thing to ProScript: whatever you're doing now is too late. We've had you forever, and you never had a single update. How can it be that all of a sudden you've got competition, Titan coming in with a new way of working, and now you want add-ons to try and make it similar to Titan? To me, it wasn't enough.
extracts.context: Asif recounting his response when ProScript tried to retain him after he decided to switch to Titan

extracts.quote: This is not about getting rid of stuff. This is about upskilling your staff to do the services that otherwise only a pharmacist would be doing. I run a travel clinic, a weight loss clinic, earwax microsuction. We're looking at Botox coming in. The more time we can free up, the more services we can offer.
extracts.context: Asif pushing back on the narrative that Titan replaces staff, explaining it enables service expansion

extracts.quote: We get an update every two weeks, and there'll be a new feature. It's like my Tesla -- every couple of weeks, we've got a new feature. It's brilliant.
extracts.context: Asif comparing Titan's rapid update cadence to Tesla's over-the-air updates, contrasting with ProScript's stagnation

extracts.quote: From a full nine-hour day, all the way down to maybe an hour and a bit at most. 85% of my time is pretty much free now.
extracts.context: Asif quantifying time saved on clinical checking after implementing Titan and Titan AI

extracts.quote: I come in in the morning, I've checked everything by half nine. I'll do it again at midday, any new ones. And everything that goes into the pick column, they crack on with it. I've done my job in half an hour. Something I was spending the whole day doing. It's nuts. It's absolutely nuts.
extracts.context: Asif describing his new daily clinical checking routine with Titan AI doing the bulk of the work

extracts.quote: This is a robot's job. What I'm doing right now is a robot's job. A robot can do this better than me.
extracts.context: Asif recalling what he used to say to the ACT checker at the pharmacy before Titan, about the manual checking process

extracts.quote: They'll pick up their handheld device with Titan Mobile on it, scan the patient's barcode, and it will tell them this patient is on shelf 7S. There's never been a case in a year where a patient's prescription has not been found. They've always been where they're supposed to be.
extracts.context: Asif describing how Titan Mobile eliminated the old problem of lost prescriptions and queue chaos at handout

extracts.quote: In pharmacy, apparently no one knows the alphabet. People can't put things in alphabetical order. The whole team would stop doing what they're doing and everyone would start going through the shelves to try and find this one patient's medication while that patient's waiting and the queue behind is huffing and puffing.
extracts.context: Asif describing the pre-Titan chaos of manually searching for prescriptions during handout

extracts.quote: They seem empowered. They've got more responsibility now. They have a patient -- it's not just a number now. This patient's medication hasn't come in, I need to chase that supplier. They're doing a lot more meaningful work, as opposed to things that anyone can do.
extracts.context: Asif describing how Titan changed dispensers' roles from mechanical dispensing to patient-focused responsibilities

extracts.quote: There's no printing anymore. We'd order three or four toners a month. We'd literally print off a pile of prescriptions about that big in the morning. Someone would sit there going through all the repeats, tearing them, sticking them. That process took an hour in the morning. I'm checking quicker than that now.
extracts.context: Asif describing the elimination of paper-based workflows after switching to Titan's paperless system

extracts.quote: If you're in this area and you're thinking about getting Titan, don't get it. Stick to paper and the smell of paper. If you're anywhere else, take the plunge. Honestly, the best thing ever.
extracts.context: Asif's tongue-in-cheek closing statement joking that local competitors should stay on old systems while everyone else adopts Titan

extracts.quote: We would have between 5 to 6 near misses a month easily on ProScript. I've had 2 since we've had Titan. And that's in a year. And they have been human errors again. Now I have zero worries. Honestly it's the best thing that's happened.
extracts.context: Asif from Safy's Chemist comparing near miss rates: 5-6 per month on ProScript vs 2 in an entire year on Titan.

extracts.quote: The barcode is never wrong, essentially. It's like a triple check. As a PMR system it's complete. More contractors should look into implementing Titan because it's more effective and it's more safer. Barcode checking means mistakes are basically not happening.
extracts.context: Cab, a locum pharmacist on his first day using Titan at a busy 10,000+ item branch, expressing confidence in the barcode validation system after only six hours of use.

extracts.quote: It's like going from a Nokia 3310 to when the first Apple iPhone came out. That's how intuitive Titan is. Claiming is very easy. It's very accurate. You could even go completely paperless.
extracts.context: Cameron, a pharmacist who has used multiple PMR systems across Lloyds, independents, and ProScript, using a technology generation metaphor to describe the leap.

extracts.quote: Picking stock, you can literally pick up to 50 patients in one go. It gives you a pick sheet. So if I'm going to the shelf, I'll only go to that shelf once for all 50 patients. I won't be picking 15 amlodipines separately, back and forth. Frees up so much staff time.
extracts.context: Cameron explaining how batch flow's consolidated picking eliminates repetitive trips to the same shelf, enabling a single staff member to dispense hundreds of items in a morning.

extracts.quote: You can scale your dispensing quite significantly without increasing the man hours, which is brilliant, because everyone knows pharmacy is quite tight on funding. You don't have the resources to just over-hire staff.
extracts.context: Cameron connecting Titan's batch flow efficiency directly to the industry funding crisis, framing it as a way to grow volume without proportionally growing payroll.

extracts.quote: We were broken into. Our shop was absolutely destroyed. Computers smashed, all the stock destroyed. I messaged the team, urgent, need your help. These guys, on a Saturday, they got it all set up for me within six, seven hours. No other PMR system would do that on a Saturday.
extracts.context: Cameron describing an emergency where his pharmacy was vandalised and the Titan implementation team rebuilt the entire system from scratch on a Saturday, getting the pharmacy back operational same day.

extracts.quote: Which PMR were you using before? Cegedim. Do you miss it? No, not at all. This is great. I love it. It's so much easier.
extracts.context: Charlie, a dispenser, describing the switch from Cegedim to Titan on training day.

extracts.quote: I actually can't believe how much I didn't know, and just how much more now I know. It's just easy. I feel like we can do this now.
extracts.context: Charlie expressing a confidence breakthrough after on-site Titan training, moving from uncertainty to empowerment.

extracts.quote: Would you go back to your old PMR system? No, thank you. It's so much more efficient. You free up a lot of time for your pharmacist. Just quicker in, quick out.

extracts.quote: A couple of hours ago, you were really scared with the change. Absolutely loving it. It's a quick, seriously quick process, enjoying it. I'm converted.
extracts.context: Dee describing her transformation from batch flow anxiety to enthusiastic adoption within hours on day one.

extracts.quote: When I started here we were on ProScript which was really difficult to use compared to Titan.
extracts.context: Emma, dispensing manager at Malpas Brook Pharmacy, directly comparing the difficulty of ProScript to Titan.

extracts.quote: You can see exactly where everything is on the board so you're not spending loads of time looking for prescriptions. So it saves time for patients when they're coming in. They haven't got to be waiting around.
extracts.context: Emma explaining how Titan's board visibility eliminated prescription hunting and reduced patient wait times.

extracts.quote: Simple really, just go onto Titan 'cause it's just so easy to use.

extracts.quote: We're doing between 25 to 27,000 items at Malpas and 12 to 13,000 items at Malpas Brook currently a month. What's particularly pleasing is that one didn't take from the other because we're so close. We've grown. So I'm delighted.
extracts.context: Geoff sharing volume numbers for both pharmacies, noting that despite being only 0.6 miles apart, the new pharmacy grew independently without cannibalising the original.

extracts.quote: Even though we're manically busy at times, it's safe. Everything gets scanned, and if it's not right, it'll alert you. It connects everything together using the best of technology. It makes things fast, safe and efficient.
extracts.context: Geoff summarising the core value proposition of Titan's barcode-based safety system in high-volume pharmacies.

extracts.quote: I was with ProScript and ProScript Connect, and I just found them clumpy, really. They were always playing catch up. Other systems, something's developed and they'll try and catch up with it, whereas Titan tends to be a leader in the market.
extracts.context: Geoff comparing his previous PMR system directly with Titan, noting ProScript's reactive approach versus Titan's innovation leadership.

extracts.quote: To be at the forefront of a leading PMR supplier really helps me know that going into the future, I'm not going to be left behind. My competitors aren't going to develop technologies that are on another level from where I'm at. I'm with the people who are going to be setting that.
extracts.context: Geoff explaining why he values Titan's innovation culture, framing his PMR choice as a competitive strategy decision rather than just an operational one.

extracts.quote: Before Titan, things felt very heavy and demanding. As you're growing, the demand for the pharmacist to be at the end of everything, you were the funnel, so everything was coming at you for you to check. A lot of pressure. So it was hard work and it was getting harder.
extracts.context: Geoff describing the bottleneck effect of the traditional dispensing model where the pharmacist must final-check every item, creating unsustainable pressure as volumes grew.

extracts.quote: Titan has really freed me up. I get my weekends back, because I was losing those. So many pharmacists do, having to work on to catch up with the workload. There's a pressure to work on after you lock the doors. I never do that, but I used to.
extracts.context: Geoff describing how the clinical check workflow in Titan removed the bottleneck of the pharmacist doing final checks on every item, which previously forced him to work evenings and weekends.

extracts.quote: You could kill yourself trying to get a wide range of customers, be overwhelmed and not have time to do any of the services. Titan releases you so it helps you grow your customer base but you're then free to go and address your customers and increase your service potential.
extracts.context: Geoff describing the pharmacy paradox of needing volume for services revenue but being crushed by dispensing workload, and how Titan breaks that cycle.

extracts.quote: We didn't realise we needed Titan until we had it, really. Our old system is all we knew. Until you take that step, you don't get the difference. Now that we've used Titan, going back is untenable. You'd never think of going back to another system.
extracts.context: Geoff articulating the 'you don't know what you don't know' barrier that keeps pharmacies on legacy systems, and how the contrast after switching makes return unthinkable.

extracts.quote: Batch flow is brilliant. Since they switched batch flow on at Malpas Brook, they've been able to organise the dispensing far better. It's made it much more efficient. extracts.context: Geoff praising batch flow for transforming a busy 12,000+ item dispensary, enabling colour-coded basket tracking that eliminated the chaos of locating patient prescriptions.

extracts.quote: The number of dispensing errors is greatly reduced. It's a fraction of what it was. It's easy to miss amlodipine for amitriptyline, but you scan them and it will tell you.
extracts.context: Geoff explaining how barcode scanning catches look-alike drug errors that were previously a significant risk in high-volume dispensing.

extracts.quote: I used to go home worrying sometimes, going over in my head thinking, oh, I hope I checked that right, because it all hinged on you at the final check. But this way it's all released and the system is going to pick it up. It's always taken a weight off my shoulders.
extracts.context: Geoff reflecting on the anxiety he used to carry home after work under the old PMR system where all final checks depended solely on the pharmacist.

extracts.quote: If you said to me when I took the pharmacy over in 2003 with two and a half thousand items, how would you cope with 25,000? I'd worry about it. extracts.context: Geoff reflecting on 10x growth from 2,500 to 25,000 items per month over his ownership period, crediting Titan's scalability for making that growth manageable.

extracts.quote: The staff feel more engaged, more involved, more trusted, even though it is with a very good system underpinning what they do. As long as the standard operating procedures are being followed, it's pretty much failsafe.
extracts.context: Geoff describing the positive cultural change among dispensary staff who now complete prescriptions end-to-end rather than just bringing baskets to the pharmacist for final checking.

extracts.quote: We've got 40 staff. It's grown. But I have to say it's an exciting, cohesive team. They all have their different areas and excel in them, which is why we're growing. It's huge and still growing. That's the buzz you want. That kind of momentum.

extracts.quote: We've now got three consultation rooms. I'll have five functioning consultation rooms so we can literally be a health centre where we will have independent prescribers and ACTs running services every hour of the day from nine till six.

extracts.quote: Don't just look at it, get on board. Because otherwise that ship will sail. You'll be left behind, potentially. And no one wants to be left behind.

extracts.quote: Definitely the handout of EDOs. We can tell people what's in the packages, if it's not already on the shelf, where it is in the process. And knowing you've got items in the fridge or CD cupboard, because the amount of times we used to not give out fridge items is a big, big thing.

extracts.context: Ian describing how Titan enables his career transition from dispensary-bound pharmacist to independent prescriber, with the dispensary running autonomously on day one.

extracts.quote: Today, when I have done circa 50 flu jabs -- that's not loads, but there would still be, at four or five o'clock when there's no more flu jabs, piles and piles of baskets waiting for me to check. That's not the case today, even on our first day. It's just gone on smooth in a way that it couldn't have done before.
extracts.context: Ian, a pharmacist, describing how Titan eliminated the end-of-day checking backlog that used to follow a flu clinic.

extracts.quote: I'm quite hopeful that my role is going to change completely and it will allow me to be in here rather than dispensing.
extracts.context: Ian envisioning his future role as consultation-focused rather than dispensing-focused, enabled by Titan.

extracts.quote: It's been really good seeing the visibility of where each prescription is in each stage. When a patient comes in, it's been really easy to find that and get it checked and out to the patient ASAP.
extracts.context: Ivan describing the prescription tracking visibility on day two of using Titan at Rexall Chemist. Also in post transcript.

extracts.quote: My best feature so far is the visibility of all the Owings on one page, and seeing where they are, and being able to update the status for each item so the entire team can see where it's coming from. So it's not just me.
extracts.context: Ivan, who manages stock ordering, praising the shared owings visibility that distributes information across the whole team. Also in post transcript.

extracts.quote: On average it's about one in 12,000 items that mistakes reach the customer. With this system it's one in 65,000.
extracts.context: James, a pharmacist on his first go-live day at an Avicenna branch in Portishead, quoting error rate statistics shared during training that helped him trust the clinical-check-upfront workflow.

extracts.quote: What I felt at one o'clock compared to what I felt at nine o'clock is vastly different. And even though it's half past five, I feel much better even again. I couldn't believe how quickly I did the clinical checks.
extracts.context: James reflecting on his emotional journey through his first full day using Titan, going from anxiety at 9am to genuine surprise and relief by end of day.

extracts.quote: The old one is outdated, it feels like after using the Titan. I like the bulk picking particularly, it gives us a sheet of what items we need to pick, in alphabetical order. It's really easy and saves a lot of time.
extracts.context: James on day one comparing his old PMR (Analyst) unfavourably to Titan's batch flow pick sheets.

extracts.quote: Now I know whether it's been already bagged and ready to hand out, or it's still in process, or still we have to get the prescription from the surgery. So it's easy to find the prescription.
extracts.context: James describing how shelf location and status tracking eliminated the old guesswork of hunting through alphabetical boxes.

extracts.quote: I can just take the phone, go around, scan the barcode of the product, order how many quantities. It's really easy. I don't have to take a pen and paper. As Titan says, it's paperless.
extracts.context: James discovering barcode-based stock ordering from the counter on his first day.

extracts.quote: It's given me a confidence as a contractor to say I can handle multiple branches. It's made me feel back as a pharmacist, rather than an IT person.
extracts.context: Jeet describing how Titan restored his professional identity and gave him confidence to expand his pharmacy group.

extracts.quote: During olden days when the phone used to ring, my heartbeat would stop and think, there must be an error, we must have done something wrong. Whereas now we are more excited to answer the phone calls, because we know we can't do anything wrong.
extracts.context: Jeet contrasting the fear of dispensing errors before Titan with the confidence the barcode-validated system now provides.

extracts.quote: All these pharmacies are never going to be called pharmacies. They're all going to be classed as a health clinic where patients would be going in to pick up a prescription, which will just be something as if you go to Asda to pick up a can of milk. But what you can get along with it is what we are trying to offer.
extracts.context: Jeet describing his vision of transforming pharmacies into health clinics where prescription collection is incidental to clinical services.

extracts.quote: Peer to peer is a brand new tool which Titan has enabled us to use, and it's amazing. If you're a part of the same group, you could technically consider sending your prescriptions to be dispensed at your other branch. With hub and spoke, you can only send it to the hub. With peer to peer, I could send any of my prescriptions to any of the branches.
extracts.context: Jeet explaining the flexibility advantage of peer to peer over traditional hub and spoke, allowing dynamic prescription routing between any branch.

extracts.quote: I had a branch with two staff, one on holiday, one on sickness, and 1000 prescriptions to dispense. And another branch with four staff members up to speed with everything, but they can't help each other out because they're 50 miles apart.
extracts.context: Jeet describing the resource imbalance problem between branches that peer to peer was designed to solve.

extracts.quote: The vision has always been dispensing should be the last thing on everybody's head, and that's what Titan has enabled us to do. It just tells us, don't worry about dispensing. We'll look after it.
extracts.context: Jeet articulating his strategic goal of making dispensing invisible so staff can focus entirely on patient-facing clinical services.

extracts.quote: We looked at how many items they were labelling, and we realised they were doing about on average between 12 to 15 items an hour. What we have now done is, by adding automation, we've made Titan even more efficient. We're looking at about between 40 to 45 items an hour. That dispenser has become four times more efficient.
extracts.context: Jeet using Power BI data to quantify how robotic automation combined with Titan increased dispenser throughput from 12-15 to 40-45 items per hour.

extracts.quote: Stock control now gives you the location of the stock, and if there is a location written on it, it's highly unlikely that it's not there. Somebody has assigned that stock with that shelf. Those kind of things have massively helped us. We've reduced our stock levels so much lower than what we used to hold for the same 40,000 items.
extracts.context: Jeet describing how shelf-location stock control eliminated ghost owings caused by dispensers not finding stock that was actually in the pharmacy.

extracts.quote: At a branch level, we have reduced about 45% of stock holding capacity by using peer to peer. That is a massive, massive saving.
extracts.context: Jeet quantifying stock reduction achieved by centralising dispensing through peer to peer, based on stock valuations.

extracts.quote: They used to get about 20 totes which they needed to unpack, whereas now they get about two. All that has just disappeared from branch level, so that they can now just keep focusing on how to provide that customer service.
extracts.context: Jeet quantifying how centralised hub dispensing reduced daily deliveries at branch level from 20 totes to 2, freeing staff for patient care.

extracts.quote: Batch flow along with the robotic automation has just completely changed the way we did our dispensing. It's just so clean, so neat. There is just one patient getting dispensed at one given point of time, no risk of contamination, no risk of putting wrong labels.
extracts.context: Jeet praising the combination of batch flow and single patient mode with robot automation for eliminating cross-contamination risk.

extracts.quote: Anybody who is not on Titan, I don't know how I can help, but if they want to help themselves, then they'll need to move.
extracts.context: Jeet delivering a blunt recommendation to pharmacies still using other PMR systems.

extracts.quote: We're hitting about a mark of around 50% at least at the minute which can be filtered through with Titan AI. So that's a big, big number.
extracts.context: Jeet estimating that Titan AI is currently handling about 50% of clinical checks at the spoke level, saving roughly an hour per three-hour session.

extracts.quote: Before we moved to Titan, I was spending my time in the branches till about 11 at night trying to clear the floor with the hope that next day is going to be a better day. I still remember those days because I had a young daughter who I don't think I've seen her grow that one year. By the time I go home, she was off to bed. By the time I moved out in the morning, she was still asleep.
extracts.context: Jeet recounting the toll pharmacy ownership took on his family life before Titan, working until 11pm nightly and missing his daughter's first year.

extracts.quote: Since the time we've had Titan, I think I've managed to become a dad as well. I've been managing to spend some time with her much more than what I would. Freeing up pharmacist time can do that -- make you a dad as well.
extracts.context: Jeet revealing the deeply personal impact of Titan on his relationship with his daughter after a year of barely seeing her.

extracts.quote: We implemented Titan on day one when we bought our new branch. We didn't even have a second thought. We did it. And day three, the dispensers were up and running with it.
extracts.context: Jeet describing the rapid onboarding when they installed Titan from scratch on a newly acquired pharmacy.

extracts.quote: The role-based functionality gives us massive potential to train the staff correctly, because we can start ticking the box one week at a time, so that they've mastered what they learned in week one, and then we add the second functionality.
extracts.context: Jeet explaining how Titan's granular permission controls allow them to progressively unlock features for new starters, making training safer and more structured.

extracts.quote: It's been a life changer from all perspective -- as a pharmacist, as a contractor, as a dad, as a husband. Titan has given us our life back.
extracts.context: Jeet summarising the total impact of Titan across every dimension of his life.

extracts.quote: People used to shy away from buying pharmacies. We are now thinking we can get more pharmacies, and if it's a non-Titan PMR, we're definitely getting it, because we're getting that converted.
extracts.context: Jeet explaining how Titan has reversed his acquisition strategy from cautious to aggressive, specifically targeting non-Titan pharmacies for conversion.

extracts.quote: During the olden days when the phone used to ring, my heartbeat would stop and think, 'There must be an error. We must've done something wrong.' Whereas now we are more excited to answer the phone calls because we know we can't do anything wrong. So it's more about having the confidence to see what's in that phone call. It could be a clinical service opportunity.
extracts.context: Jeet describing the dramatic shift from phone anxiety to phone excitement after switching to Titan.

extracts.quote: From all perspectives, as a pharmacist, as a contractor, as a dad, as a husband, it's been a life-changer, and that's what Titan has done for us. It's just given us our life back.
extracts.context: Jeet delivering one of the most emotionally powerful Titan endorsements, connecting professional and personal identity.

extracts.quote: It makes it nice and seamless to be using the one system. We can already see how it's going to save us an immense amount of time, not just me, but the dispensary staff, to get processes done quicker. Prescriptions ready for patients quicker, which means we're happy, patients are happy.
extracts.context: Jimrac (Chirag) on go-live day at his pharmacy, quantifying the team-wide time savings he's already seeing.

extracts.quote: I must have called the Titan implementation team double digit times on my phone. Literally pick up instantaneously. They're able to log into the system, fix the problem or do the training online. There's nothing I've asked them that they've not been able to show me or fix instantaneously.
extracts.context: Jimrac praising Titan's support responsiveness compared to other companies where you're on hold for ages.

extracts.quote: 100% gives me so much more time to do services, less stress, which is always great for your mental health as well. But most importantly, allows me to do what I love, which is speak to patients, serve the patients.
extracts.context: Jimrac connecting Titan's efficiency gains to both mental health benefits and professional fulfilment.

extracts.quote: If you're able to get yourself on board with Titan, I think it's the future of working for pharmacy, in my opinion. It uses tech, it makes processes seamless, it streamlines them.
extracts.context: Jimrac's unprompted forward-looking endorsement of Titan as the future of pharmacy work.

extracts.quote: Since day one, it's a brand new business for me. Titan makes me do a lot of other services and generate revenue. I have my personal time. I have time to do a lot of other things. I'm only doing my clinical checks, and I leave the rest for my dispensing team.
extracts.context: Kanav, a pharmacy owner with a new build pharmacy, explaining that he built his entire business model around Titan from day one, enabling multiple service streams from the start.

extracts.quote: All you do is click on one claim and it claims all the prescriptions for the day. The last pharmacy I worked at used to claim prescriptions all day long and get behind dispensing. But I don't do claiming here.
extracts.context: A conversation between Kanav and his staff member Kaya, contrasting Titan's one-click claiming with the manual claiming process at other pharmacies that consumed entire days.

extracts.quote: Since day one, I've always had Titan. It lets me do a lot of other services and generate revenue, purely because of the way Titan works, the way it's designed. And I have my personal time. I have time to do a lot of other things.
extracts.context: Kanav explaining that his brand new pharmacy was built from scratch with Titan, enabling a services-first model from day one.

extracts.quote: On a daily basis, I'm only doing my clinical checks, and I leave the rest for my dispensing team to dispense it, bag it, file it and hand it out. Meanwhile, I do all my other services in the consultation rooms.
extracts.context: Kanav describing his daily workflow where his pharmacist role is almost entirely services-focused.

extracts.quote: Through Titan, all you do is click on one claim, and it claims all the prescriptions for the day. So then you're free to do dispensing, free to do all the other things. Which is why we have a lot of time to do other things, other than just keep scanning prescriptions all day long.
extracts.context: Kanav explaining how Titan's one-click claiming replaced the tedious manual claiming process at other pharmacies.

extracts.quote: I've had really good response from the community saying your services are really efficient, and that's purely because of Titan, the way it works, the way it lets me do what I need to do.
extracts.context: Kanav sharing community feedback about his pharmacy's efficiency, attributing it directly to Titan.

extracts.quote: The barcode validation when you dispense it -- do you think there's room for errors? No. I think it's fine. I'm enjoying it.
extracts.context: Kate, a dispenser at Rexall Chemist, confirming that barcode scanning during packaging gives her confidence in accuracy.

extracts.quote: So would you go back to ProScript? Just getting it done a lot quicker.
extracts.context: Katie, a dispenser, dismissing a return to ProScript after her first batch flow session, citing speed.

extracts.quote: Before I was using Titan, I was working two or three nights a week late. I was stressed, burnt out. I just didn't have the capacity. Now I get home every night on time. I even work from home several days a week. It's just changed everything.
extracts.context: Kieran, pharmacy owner in Tamworth, describing the dramatic before-and-after transformation in his work-life balance since adopting Titan.

extracts.quote: Our NMS have gone from 30 to 180 a month, and all our other services, private and NHS, have all done likewise. My staff, my patients, are all happier.
extracts.context: Kieran quantifying a 6x increase in New Medicine Service completions after adopting Titan, attributing it to pharmacist time freed from dispensing.

extracts.quote: My staff run my dispensary. I don't go in it anymore. They shout at me if I go in. I don't have to deal with the mundane of running that side of the business because they do it all for me now.
extracts.context: Kieran describing how Titan empowered his dispenser staff to fully own the dispensary workflow, allowing him to focus entirely on clinical services.

extracts.quote: If you're on the fence, go see a pharmacy. Check it out, see how it works for real, and then get ready to hand your notice in at your current PMR.
extracts.context: Kieran's closing call-to-action, delivered with confidence after describing his transformation from burnt-out to thriving.

extracts.quote: The main concern we had with ProScript was the near misses. So it's the accuracy checking which was the main reason why we chose Titan. And the second reason is freeing up the pharmacist time so we can focus on services and generate more income.
extracts.context: Krishna from Clifton Pharmacy explaining the two primary reasons for switching from ProScript to Titan.

extracts.quote: Been ProScript through and through for the last 10-15 years. The transition was, has to be expected, quite hard to begin with, but everybody took it on board, and I think going forward, it would be great.
extracts.context: Lauren, an ACT and manager, describing the transition from 15 years of ProScript to Titan.

extracts.quote: The training's been great. We've got a few members of staff that are not so tech savvy. So to have all these new systems and computers and devices in place, it's been a bit daunting for some of them, but having the guys on hand to help with that has been really useful.
extracts.context: Lauren describing how on-site training helped less tech-confident staff get comfortable with Titan.

extracts.quote: I have locumed in other pharmacies and they were all paper-based. If a patient came in, you would give them waiting time of 15 to 20 minutes. Here you can locate the prescription straight away and get it dispensed, checked and handed out within five minutes.
extracts.context: Maliha comparing her locum experience in paper-based pharmacies with Titan's speed, a 75% reduction in patient wait time.

extracts.quote: The audit trail is a lifesaver to me. You know exactly who's done that prescription, what time it was done. I'd go back and I'd know exactly where I'm at. I wouldn't need to ask a staff member what's happened.
extracts.context: Maliha naming the audit trail as her single most valued feature for maintaining oversight without micromanagement.

extracts.quote: Barcode scanning makes the process more streamlined. Anything you scan will get flagged on the system if it was an incorrect item. There's less pressure on the pharmacist to catch these errors.
extracts.context: Maliha explaining how barcode verification acts as another safety layer, reducing pharmacist error anxiety.

extracts.quote: With Titan batch, especially with care homes, once one care home drops, we put it into a batch and process that care home together. It's much quicker and easier to see on the board where the prescriptions are.
extracts.context: Maliha explaining how batch processing simplifies the handling of their 30 care homes' prescriptions.

extracts.quote: We barely did any NMS while we were on ProScript. But now with Titan, we can do up to 300 if not more than that per month. Titan has freed up a lot of space in terms of my workload.
extracts.context: Maliha attributing their NMS volume growth from near-zero to 300+ monthly directly to Titan's time savings.

extracts.quote: Titan AI is doing about 70% of the clinical checking. Where things are done more quickly, more efficiently, sometimes I don't have to look at that prescription at all. My workload has reduced dramatically.
extracts.context: Maliha quantifying how much of the clinical checking burden Titan AI now handles, freeing her from the bench.

extracts.quote: With Titan AI, it's like a second pair of eyes. On busy days or when I'm doing services, I can just switch it on and leave it to check prescriptions for me.
extracts.context: Maliha describing the peace of mind Titan AI provides, particularly when she's pulled away for clinical services.

extracts.quote: Previously with ProScript, I'd have my bench fill up probably every hour, and I'd be signing off my bench the whole day, just checking, which was boring, and there would always be that fear of, have I checked that properly? Do I need to recheck it?
extracts.context: Maliha describing the repetitive drudgery and constant anxiety of manual clinical checking under ProScript.

extracts.quote: Previously, there'd be times where I'd have to stay behind just to get the work done. But now, if I finish at 4:30 I go home at 4:30. I wouldn't even stay for a minute extra.
extracts.context: Maliha describing the personal impact of Titan on her daily schedule, no more unpaid overtime to clear the bench.

extracts.quote: When I'm not in the pharmacy, I want to just spend time with my child. Previously there'd be times where I'd have to stay behind. But now if I finish at 4:30 I go home at 4:30.
extracts.context: Maliha connecting the on-time finish enabled by Titan to her personal life as a parent.

extracts.quote: The biggest thing that Titan has changed for me is workload. If somebody was thinking about switching to Titan, I'd say go for it. It's a game changer.
extracts.context: Maliha's closing endorsement, choosing workload reduction as Titan's single most important impact.

extracts.quote: I feel quite positive about it. I think it's a lot easier to use. I feel it just gives you that reassurance that everything is correct. Change is difficult, but you guys have done brilliant, smashed it today.
extracts.context: Maria on day one of Titan training, expressing cautious optimism and gratitude to the training team.

extracts.quote: This system reduces dispensing errors to virtually zero. That is one of the most important things that any pharmacy would appreciate. If you can knock down your dispensing errors, that is your biggest risk, and Titan has allowed us to do that.
extracts.context: Mustafa, a multi-site pharmacy owner at Silverwood and Mountain pharmacies, describing the safety impact of Titan's barcode validation system after being initially sceptical.

extracts.quote: For years since Titan was launched, I've been very sceptical of Titan. I went through a demo a couple of years ago and felt the software wasn't quite ready. But now, a few years down the line, it's come leaps and bounds. We can work from different locations. That's really good from a pharmacist point of view.
extracts.context: Mustafa describing his journey from sceptic to advocate, noting the maturity of the platform and the remote clinical checking capability as a turning point.

extracts.quote: It's taken away a massive bottleneck. The whole dispensing process is turned on its head. Previously the staff would dispense, stock the items, then the pharmacist would clinical and accuracy check at the end. That bottleneck where they're waiting for the pharmacist is gone.
extracts.context: Mustafa explaining how Titan's front-loaded clinical checking eliminated the traditional workflow bottleneck that kept dispensary staff waiting for the pharmacist.

extracts.quote: No other PMR system does that. The fact that you take on feedback from the users so that the programmers can then update the programming is brilliant.
extracts.context: Mustafa singling out Titan's user feedback loop as unique in the market, praising how user input directly shapes product development.

extracts.quote: The rollout itself has gone really well. Not without its hurdles, not without its speed bumps and stressful moments. We need to be honest. But actually, on the whole, really happy with how it's landed, how the teams have adapted to it. 22 branches, the whole region is now done, and I'm excited now about what we can do next.
extracts.context: Nathan, a regional manager overseeing 22 pharmacy stores, reflecting on completing a full-region Titan rollout on the final go-live day.

extracts.quote: Any change of PMR is difficult. That's probably the reason pharmacies only do it every 20 years. But if the teams come into it with the right attitude and come in on the front foot, that is absolutely vital to landing it the way you want.
extracts.context: Nathan sharing wisdom from rolling out Titan across 22 branches, noting that staff mindset is the key success factor in PMR transitions.

extracts.quote: I've used Pharmacy Manager for about 26 years. I was a bit reluctant. But constantly using it, it just becomes second nature now. From day one to week six, there's been a massive improvement. We went through a checklist today and I was surprised how many ticks we had.
extracts.context: Nicola, a long-tenured dispenser who had only ever used one PMR system for 26 years, describing her transition to Titan and the progress she discovered during a site visit checklist review.

extracts.quote: I like the repeat flow. It's going to save this pharmacy, because most of the time we order stuff for people and we don't know what's coming back until the customer complains.
extracts.context: Ola, pharmacist at Ringwood Pharmacy, explaining how repeat flow solved the visibility problem of not knowing which repeat prescriptions were returning until patients complained about missing items.

extracts.quote: I've had a lot of people come visit the pharmacy to see our layout, to see how we work. They're really, really shocked that I can spend a whole hour with them and not be interrupted and still get the work done and not stay in the evening.
extracts.context: Prab describing how visiting pharmacists are amazed that he has a full hour free during operating hours while running nearly 16,000 items monthly.

extracts.quote: The AI is currently checking and clearing about 70% of the prescriptions that we receive. So the volume that I need to review and check is really small, and I can actually then spend some time actually looking at why these prescriptions have been rejected by the AI.
extracts.context: Prab quantifying Titan AI's clearance rate and explaining how it shifts his role from bulk checking to focused clinical review.

extracts.quote: As soon as I took over on day one, I knew that I did not want to have any other PMR other than Titan in here. So on day one, we started with Titan.
extracts.context: Prab describing his conviction in choosing Titan from the very first day of owning his pharmacy in 2021.

extracts.quote: On the old system, Mr. Jones might walk into the pharmacy and I'd look on the system, I'd say yes, he's got a prescription, and I'd look in this old file box. Flick through the file. Oh, his prescription is not in the file. Is it being done? No. Is it with the owings? So we no longer have that issue anymore.
extracts.context: Prab acting out the frustrating guesswork of locating a patient's prescription on his previous PMR system.

extracts.quote: One of the other features I think is incredibly underrated is that when patients collect, we're capturing their exemption information at that point. So end of month claim process is so easy -- one click on claim all and everything gets sent.
extracts.context: Prab explaining how Titan captures exemption data at handout, making NHS claiming a single-click process.

extracts.quote: End of month claim process is so easy, one click on claim all and everything gets sent. There's no more having to manually scan through your prescriptions to send your claims off. That's a huge time saver.
extracts.context: Prab highlighting how Titan automates the monthly NHS claim submission process because exemption data is captured at handout.

extracts.quote: I've shown people Titan in the past, and they described it as cavemen seeing fire for the first time. The shock to them was incredible, and they saw that actually there was a better way of working and also a safer way of working.
extracts.context: Prab recounting how visiting pharmacists reacted when they saw Titan in action for the first time.

extracts.quote: Titan has given me my work life balance back. It gives you peace of mind to know when you go home. 'Oh, did I check this correctly? Have I done this correctly?' All those worries are gone now.
extracts.context: Prab describing how Titan eliminated the nagging anxiety he used to carry home about whether prescriptions were dispensed safely.

extracts.quote: It's not just the big feature modules. It's a lot of little things in the system that really add up. The fact that on the patient flyout, we have access to the summary care record without needing to go to another website. The prescription tracker is already embedded. These small things really make a big difference.
extracts.context: Prab praising Titan's integrated micro-features like embedded SCR access and prescription tracker that eliminate tab-switching.

extracts.quote: One of the only times I've received a slightly good rating from the GPhC was the fact that I had introduced Titan into my pharmacy back in 2019. They hadn't seen a system like this at that point, and they were really impressed with the level of safety and the amount of information you're capturing about each prescription.
extracts.context: Prab revealing that his GPhC inspection singled out Titan as a positive finding, validating the system's safety and audit capabilities.

extracts.quote: I kind of see having the robot with Titan as more of an evolutionary step rather than revolutionary. A lot of thought's gone into this integration between Titan and Meditech. I kind of feel some of these other systems, it's like a bolt on. It's an extra part, rather than it flowing through really nicely.
extracts.context: Prab contrasting Titan's native robot integration philosophy with competitors where robotics feels like an afterthought.

extracts.quote: I think with the robot coming in, utilising Titan in a much bigger way, that's going to allow me to hopefully double my volume while maintaining the current amount of staff that I have, and also focus on continuing to provide a more patient centric service.
extracts.context: Prab projecting that Titan plus a Meditech robot will let him double his 16,000-item volume without adding headcount.

extracts.quote: To be a digital first pharmacy is all about freeing yourself up to not be bogged down by current constraints. Everything should have a purpose and have a benefit. We are 90% paperless at the moment.
extracts.context: Prab defining what digital-first pharmacy means to him and quantifying their paperless achievement.

extracts.quote: Five years ago, I would not be able to be having this conversation with you. I'd probably still be in my dispensary trying to check hundreds of baskets, being incredibly stressed and just not really enjoying pharmacy.
extracts.context: Prab reflecting on how dramatically different his working life is since adopting Titan, contrasting it with where he would have been.

extracts.quote: I think thanks to Titan PMR, I'm probably still in community pharmacy. Otherwise I would have left a long time ago, because I just think the level of stress that you have using these manual processes is just too much.
extracts.context: Prab crediting Titan with keeping him in the profession, saying he would have left community pharmacy entirely without it.

extracts.quote: I've got about five batch flow stations. They can have about 30 baskets in the meat, so we can work on 150 patients simultaneously. And that's how we can achieve the level of volume that we do with the least amount of staff.
extracts.context: Prab describing his pharmacy layout optimised around batch flow, allowing 150 simultaneous patient prescriptions with minimal staff.

extracts.quote: We can actually prioritise prescriptions in the queue. You can say, this prescription needs to be done now, we can highlight it as waiting. Similarly, you can mark them as they're coming today. And that really helps the team to structure our workload.
extracts.context: Prab describing Titan's prescription tagging and priority system that lets the team dynamically manage their daily workload.

extracts.quote: At the moment, we're doing nearly 16,000 items, and we do this without a robot. There's no chaos. Everything's really calm and really organised.
extracts.context: Prab stating his monthly volume and emphasising the calm working environment despite having no robot assistance.

extracts.quote: One of the things I really love about Titan is that it's incredibly simple. On the main screen, everything in the pharmacy just flows from the left to the right, and everyone just really understands that.
extracts.context: Prab praising Titan's intuitive left-to-right Kanban workflow that any staff member can immediately grasp.

extracts.quote: With any other PMR, I'd still be checking baskets at 8pm if I was working on my own. But with Titan, that's long gone.
extracts.context: Prab delivering a direct comparison of his old evening routine versus the freedom Titan provides.

extracts.quote: Patients often get a text while they're out walking the dog, and they pop in and it's just ready. There's no manual sort of work that needs to be done.
extracts.context: Prab describing the automatic text notification patients receive when their prescription is shelved, eliminating manual messaging.

extracts.quote: Titan is efficient, it's safe, and it lets us be patient centric without burning out the team or myself.
extracts.context: Prab delivering a concise three-point summary of Titan's value proposition.

extracts.quote: If someone's thinking about getting Titan, I would just tell them sign straight away. It's going to make a huge difference to your working life, and it's going to allow you to grow your pharmacy business and deliver the services that the NHS want in the future.
extracts.context: Prab giving his direct recommendation to pharmacists considering Titan.

extracts.quote: With my previous PMR, Mr. Jones would come in, I'd look up on the system, yes I have a prescription. Then I'd look at this old box file, go through the file -- is it here?
